items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: we had an influx of young drummers that came in - Kansas Fields. ... Of course I do. He went to Paris.

ctx.x: I think he's in Chicago now, right?

Yes. Kansas, when he came back from Europe, went to my friend Oliver, O. J. That's where he stayed. Now you see, Milt, we must remember this. Since I took to the drums I found out that the drummer was the key. The drummer was the key; this was the heartbeat of the body of music. Now we all have individual lives to live. A lot of us were not allowed the privilege to play with whom we wanted to play with. We had to do what we had to do. That's the one instrument that has nothing to do with race, color, or creed,…

years ago, this year, any time. But when the peoples that sit down in percussion, when they do these different things they have to do what they have to do. Now when peoples get out here and get just a little name they place them in a certain position and it's the drum that is the key. You see, he's got to sit there like the heart of the body and ho, not used but utilized. As I reiterated before, could you imagine what would have happened had a Gene Krupa or a Buddy Rich or a Shelly Manne had had a chance to play…
